1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module nineteen: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser. This module covers quick-reference recap and service chooser. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. See the whole data platform on one page. Use the service choosers to turn a requirement into a service. Review the look-alike services that the exam uses as distractors. Recall the numbers and rules worth memorizing. --.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight, Start to Finish
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight, Start to Finish. Ingest truck telemetry (streams) and order files (batch). Store raw data in S three, serving data in Redshift and DynamoDB. Catalog it, transform it, orchestrate it, monitor it. Secure and govern every step. Your job: recall which service owns which step.

1.title: The Whole Pipeline on One Page
1.text: The Whole Pipeline on One Page. The figure shows this: A reference data platform: ingest, store and catalog, transform, serve, with orchestration across the flow and monitoring and security around it.

1.title: Service Chooser by Requirement
1.text: Service Chooser by Requirement. Exam tip: Read the requirement word first (cost, overhead, latency, security, near real time), then pick the service from the chooser that owns that word.

1.title: Ingestion
1.text: Ingestion. SaaS data (Salesforce, Zendesk, S A P) into S three or Redshift, no code. Amazon AppFlow. Database copy or ongoing replication (C D C). A W S D M S (Database Migration Service). Custom, replayable stream, many consumers, per-key order. Kinesis Data Streams. Load a stream into S three, Redshift, OpenSearch with no code. Amazon Data Firehose. Existing Kafka workloads. Amazon M S K (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Table change feed from DynamoDB. DynamoDB Streams. S F T P (Secure File Transfer Protocol) partners into S three. A W S Transfer Family. On-premises file shares into A W S. A W S DataSync. Offline bulk transfer. A W S Snow Family. Third-party datasets. A W S Data Exchange. Start on arrival of a file. S three Event Notifications or EventBridge.

1.title: Ingestion, continued
1.text: Ingestion, continued. Start on a time. EventBridge Scheduler, Glue scheduled trigger.

1.title: Transform and process
1.text: Transform and process. Serverless Spark E T L (extract, transform, load) with a catalog. A W S Glue. Control of Hadoop and Spark versions, very large clusters. Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce) (Serverless for no cluster). Small event-driven transformation. A W S Lambda. S Q L transformations in the warehouse. Redshift (E L T). S Q L E T L on S three. Athena C T A S (create table as select) and insert into. Visual, no-code preparation. A W S Glue DataBrew. Stateful stream processing. Managed Service for Apache Flink. Containers for custom code. E C S (Elastic Container Service) or E K S (Elastic Kubernetes Service) (Fargate), A W S Batch for many jobs. L L M (large language model) processing of text at scale. Bedrock batch inference.

1.title: Orchestrate and automate
1.text: Orchestrate and automate. Serverless multi-service workflow with retries, branches, approval. Step Functions. Existing Airflow D A G s (directed acyclic graph). Amazon M W A A (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow). Glue-only chain. Glue workflows. Route events and schedule. EventBridge (bus, Pipes, Scheduler). Alerts and fan-out. S N S (Simple Notification Service); buffer with S Q S (Simple Queue Service).

1.title: Store
1.text: Store. Data lake, any format, cheap. Amazon S three (Parquet; S three Tables or Iceberg for tables). Analytics warehouse. Amazon Redshift. Key lookups at scale, single-digit ms. Amazon DynamoDB. Relational transactions. R D S (Relational Database Service) or Aurora. Durable in-memory, microsecond reads. Amazon MemoryDB. Graph. Amazon Neptune. Search, logs, vectors. Amazon OpenSearch Service. Vector search in PostgreSQL. Aurora PostgreSQL plus pgvector (H N S W).

1.title: Catalog, quality, analysis
1.text: Catalog, quality, analysis. Technical catalog shared by engines. Glue Data Catalog ( plus crawlers). Business catalog, glossary, subscriptions. SageMaker Catalog. Data quality rules. Glue Data Quality (D Q D L), DataBrew rulesets. S Q L on S three. Amazon Athena. B I (business intelligence) dashboards. QuickSight (Amazon Quick). Operational time series. Managed Grafana.

1.title: Operate, secure, govern
1.text: Operate, secure, govern. Metrics and alarms. CloudWatch. Who called the A P I. CloudTrail (data events for objects), CloudTrail Lake. Configuration history and compliance. A W S Config. Credentials with rotation. Secrets Manager. Keys. A W S K M S (Key Management Service) (customer managed for control and sharing). Central lake permissions. Lake Formation (L F-tags, filters). Find P I I (personally identifiable information) in S three. Amazon Macie. Central backups. A W S Backup. Region restrictions. S C P s (service control policy) (the requested Region condition).

1.title: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart
1.text: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart. Exam tip: When two look-alikes both seem to work, the question names the difference: replay, serverless, no code, existing Kafka or Airflow, or who made the call.

1.title: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued
1.text: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued. Kinesis Data Streams versus Data Firehose. Streams: you build consumers, replay, ordering by key. Firehose: delivers to a destination, no replay. Kinesis versus M S K. A W S-native shards versus Apache Kafka; M S K for existing Kafka. Glue versus E M R. Glue: serverless E T L, catalog. E M R: control, ecosystem, huge scale. Glue versus Lambda. Glue: large Spark jobs. Lambda: small, fifteen-minute, event-driven. Athena versus Redshift. Athena: serverless S Q L on S three, pay per data scanned. Redshift: warehouse for heavy, repeated, concurrent analytics. Redshift Spectrum versus federated query. Spectrum: files in S three. Federated: live R D S or Aurora.

1.title: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued
1.text: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued. Step Functions versus M W A A. Serverless state machines versus managed Airflow D A G s. Glue workflows versus Step Functions. Glue-only versus any A W S service. S N S versus S Q S. Publish or subscribe push versus queue pull. EventBridge bus versus Pipes. Many-to-many routing versus point-to-point with filter and enrichment. DynamoDB versus R D S. Key-based, schemaless, scales out versus joins and transactions. DynamoDB versus MemoryDB. Serverless key-value store versus durable in-memory, microsecond reads. H N S W (Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds) versus I V F (inverted file). Graph index, high recall, more memory versus clusters, faster build, less memory. Secrets Manager versus Parameter Store. Rotation, per-secret charge versus configuration, free standard tier.

1.title: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued
1.text: Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart, continued. S S E (server-side encryption)-S three versus S S E-K M S. Default, no key control versus your key, audit, sharing. I A M (Identity and Access Management) role versus user. Temporary credentials for workloads versus long-term credentials. R B A C (role-based access control) versus T B A C (tag-based access control) versus A B A C (attribute-based access control). By role versus by resource tag versus compare principal and resource attributes. CloudWatch versus CloudTrail versus Config. Metrics and logs versus A P I calls (who) versus resource configuration history. Glue Data Catalog versus SageMaker Catalog. Technical versus business catalog. DataBrew versus Glue Data Quality. Visual rules for analysts versus D Q D L (Data Quality Definition Language) rules for engineers.

1.title: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering
1.text: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering. Exam. sixty-five questions (fifty scored), one hundred thirty minutes, seven hundred twenty of one thousand, domains thirty-four or twenty-six or twenty-two or eighteen. Kinesis Data Streams. Shard write one megabytes per second or one thousand records per second, read two megabytes per second shared; retention twenty-four hours to three hundred sixty-five days; enhanced fan-out consumers twenty. Firehose. S three buffer default five mebibytes or three hundred s (interval zero to nine hundred s). DynamoDB. Item four hundred kilobytes; P I T R (point-in-time recovery) thirty-five days; T T L (time to live) deletes within a few days. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

1.title: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering, continued
1.text: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering, continued. Lambda. fifteen min; one hundred twenty-eight to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes; or tmp five hundred twelve to ten thousand two hundred forty megabytes; default one thousand concurrency. A P I Gateway. ten thousand rps default, five thousand burst. Step Functions. Standard: one year, exactly once; Express: five min, at least once. S three lifecycle. less than one hundred twenty-eight kilobytes not transitioned by default; minimum durations thirty or ninety or one hundred eighty days. Redshift. copy from many files (multiple of slices); key or all or even or auto; Data A P I results twenty-four h. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

1.title: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering, continued
1.text: Numbers and Rules Worth Remembering, continued. Glue. D P U (data processing unit) equals four virtual C P Us plus sixteen gigabytes; retries zero to ten; bookmarks default disabled; trigger starts two crawlers. K M S. Rotation three hundred sixty-five days (customer managed), deletion wait seven to thirty days; A W S managed keys cannot be shared. CloudTrail. Event history ninety days; data events off by default; Lake closed to new customers from thirty-one May two thousand twenty-six. Exam tip: Memorize the shapes of the limits (which service has which kind of limit) before the exact numbers, and check the A W S page for any number tagged Verify live. This fact moves with the A W S pages, so check the current value before you rely on it.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Method: Read the requirement word (cost, overhead, latency, security, near real time), match the service, eliminate look-alikes. Ingestion: SaaS AppFlow; D B (database) D M S; stream Kinesis or M S K or Firehose; S F T P Transfer Family; incremental bookmarks or C D C (change data capture). Transformation: Glue (serverless), E M R (control), Lambda (small), Athena C T A S; Parquet plus partition plus compact. Orchestration: Step Functions (serverless), M W A A (Airflow), Glue workflows, EventBridge; retry, D L Q (dead-letter queue), idempotent. Stores: S three, Redshift, DynamoDB, R D S or Aurora, MemoryDB, Neptune, OpenSearch; Iceberg; H N S W or I V F. Catalog and lifecycle: Glue Data Catalog plus crawlers; lifecycle rules, versioning, T T L, unload; A W S Backup. Operations: CloudWatch metrics or logs or alarms to S N S; CloudTrail who; Config what changed; Glue D Q (data quality) or DataBrew quality. Security: Roles not keys, Secrets Manager, Lake Formation, K M S, T L S (Transport Layer Security), Macie, S C P Regions, mask or anonymize. In the next module, we continue the course.
